sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface ELISA, flow cytometry, and electrophysiology confirmed normal surface trafficking and channel function; L12 states explicitly 'no impact on channel folding, trafficking, or function'.
sites.rationale: Six independent ledger lines (L1–L7, L12–L13) all pin the identical junction: after E146 (Glu146), before Q147 (Gln147), in the 11-residue S1–S2 extracellular loop (topology span 144–154). Python confirms residue 146 = E and residue 147 = Q, matching the papers exactly. The junction is 3 residues from the TM1 C-terminus (143) and 9 residues from the TM2 N-terminus (155), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-clearance rule. No cysteines or N-glycosylation sequons are present in the loop. L12 provides the strongest validation: folding, trafficking, and function all confirmed preserved. Full-length human KCNQ1 (membrane-anchored, not a secreted ectodomain) was engineered with a c-Myc epitope (EQKLISEEDL) inserted after residue E146 in the S1–S2 extracellular loop. Multiple independent groups (PMC7988323, DOI:10.1101/2020.07.29.227231, PMC5842040, PMC12632771, PMC13041670, PMC12724399) report the identical junction. L12 (PMC7988323) explicitly states the modification has no impact on channel folding, trafficking, or function. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The c-myc tag (EQKLISEEDL) was inserted into the extracellular S1–S2 linker between residues Glu146 and Gln147.

sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry with Alexa 647-bungarotoxin confirmed cell-surface display of BBS-KCNQ1-YFP (L11). Electrophysiological function of the BBS-tagged construct is NOT MEASURED in the cited ledger lines.
sites.rationale: Three ledger lines (L8, L9, L10) independently report the BBS insertion between residues 148 and 149 of the S1–S2 extracellular loop. Python confirms residue 148 = Y (Tyr) and residue 149 = A (Ala), both within the extracellular span 144–154. The junction is 5 residues from TM1 (143) and 7 residues from TM2 (155), satisfying ≥3-residue clearance. No cysteines or N-glycosylation sequons are present. This is a distinct, independently validated junction 2 residues C-terminal to the myc site, demonstrating the loop tolerates insertions at multiple positions. Full-length KCNQ1 (membrane-anchored) was engineered with a 13-residue bungarotoxin-binding site (BBS) peptide inserted between residues 148 and 149 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop (PMC11429900, PMC12218124, PMC5764571). L11 confirms surface labeling of the BBS-Q1-YFP construct by Alexa 647-conjugated fluorescent bungarotoxin measured by flow cytometry. [validation: surface_only; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: A 13-residue bungarotoxin binding site peptide (BBS) sequence was introduced between sequences for residues 148 and 149 in KCNQ1 extracellular S1–S2 loop using QuikChange Lightning Site-Directed Mutagenesis kit (Stratagene) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

literature_notes: All ledger lines converge on the single extracellular loop of KCNQ1 (S1–S2 linker, topology span 144–154). Two distinct junctions are supported: after E146 (myc tag, six papers, function confirmed) and after Y148 (BBS 13-aa tag, three papers, surface confirmed). No other extracellular spans exist in KCNQ1 that carry ledger-supported insertions: the S2–S3 linker (216–220, 5 residues) and the S3–S4 linker (283–327) have no qualifying ledger lines. The intracellular C-terminus (344–676) and N-terminus (1–122) are not extracellular and were not considered. L4/L5 also mention mEGFP fused to the C-terminus of mycKCNQ1, but the C-terminus is intracellular (residue 676, topology I), so that fusion is not an extracellular site and is excluded. L13 is a general statement subsumed by L1–L7 and adds no new junction.
